memory_update.text: AMKR should remain the primary US-listed OSAT/advanced-packaging reference candidate for this node, but evidence must distinguish durable AI/HPC advanced-packaging economics from broad cyclical OSAT recovery.
CAMT is a strong underfollowed equipment candidate because inspection/metrology demand is directly tied to advanced packaging, HBM, chiplets, and hybrid bonding yield control.
FORM is an indirect test-capacity candidate: the key verification item is whether HBM and AI/HPC probe-card demand is material enough to drive revenue, margin, or backlog.
KLIC is a lower-attention advanced-packaging equipment hypothesis tied to thermocompression bonding and advanced memory packaging; it needs customer/order proof before promotion beyond Layer 1.
US-listed universe misses many important Asian OSAT and memory-backend suppliers such as Powertech; maintain non-US comps as evidence anchors while the requested universe remains US-listed.
The node should be tracked through four chokepoint sublayers: OSAT capacity, inspection/metrology yield control, probe-card/test interfaces, and bonding/assembly tools.

node: Advanced packaging, OSAT, memory backend, fan-out and test overflow
summary: Layer 1B expansion found a US-listed universe centered on OSAT capacity, inspection/metrology, probe-card test capacity, and bonding equipment. The cleanest direct public exposure is Amkor as an outsourced advanced packaging and test provider, while Camtek, FormFactor, and Kulicke & Soffa are underfollowed equipment/test picks-and-shovels tied to AI/HPC, HBM, chiplets, hybrid bonding, wafer-level packaging, or thermo-compression bonding. The key chokepoint hypothesis remains that AI/HBM demand crowds out backend capacity and raises the value of qualified packaging, inspection, probe, and bonding capacity. This is research-only universe expansion, not a trading recommendation.
